analysis.title: Dip-Buyers Went 3x Long Into The Nasdaq's Worst Month Of The Year. Who Blinks First?
key_insights: US-listed ETFs took in just over $200B in October, the second-largest month in Goldman's dataset after roughly $230B in late 2025 (both read off a chart). Year-to-date inflows are $1.7T, already above 2025's full-year total of about $1.45T.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.4% (a two standard deviation move) on Friday and had its worst month of the year, after Intel fell the most on record. ETF inflows continued anyway.

ETFs that underperformed the NDX in October took in 2.4% of their assets, three times the 0.8% that went into ETFs that beat it. Semis were the largest beneficiaries among the laggards, followed by broad tech, EM and Brazil-exposed ETFs.

Levered ETFs had their largest month of inflows in Goldman's dataset at +$13B, about 60% above the early-2025 high. This reverses a roughly $12B outflow earlier in 2026. Friday alone brought $3B, the group's largest daily inflow YTD.

On the same Friday, Nomura's McElligott warned levered ETFs faced a $35B rebalancing sale into the close. The funds' swap desks sold the underlying to reset leverage while investors bought the fund shares.

Historically, levered long ETFs take in about 50bps of prior-day AUM on days when the Nasdaq falls more than two standard deviations. Inverse ETFs see outflows on those days and about 58bps of inflows on the best days.
Goldman's Coppersmith says October saw the biggest plunge in risk appetite in 5 years. The article contrasts professionals de-risking with retail buying record triple-levered exposure.
The NDX underperformed the equal-weight S&P by roughly 12% in October, its largest monthly shortfall since 2002.

Health care gained about 10% in October, its best month since April 2020, and XLV took in $1.6B, its best month of inflows since May 2022. The article reads this as an orderly defensive rotation out of AI and megacap tech.
COPX has fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, tying the longest losing streak since the ETF launched in 2010. The Goldman desk faced supply for miners on Friday.
The EM and Brazil flow leg shows cracks. Korea saw $2.6B of retail selling last week, Brazil inflows have started to reverse after the election, and Asia has drawn $81B of retail money YTD.
ETFs were roughly 31% of the tape in the week's final session, the highest full-session level since June.

On Monday the NDX gave up an early 1% gain while oil fell more than 7% on US-Iran talk hopes, and it closed in correction, 10% below its October record. Friday's $3B of levered buying is underwater, and the 3x units built over three weeks will rebalance lower each afternoon the index falls.

The authors side with the professionals. They argue that with levered ETF buyers as the marginal bid and the Fed hiking, the next leg lower is likely to be set by the rebalancing at the close rather than by fundamentals.
earnings_insights: Intel fell the most on record at the end of October, which the article cites as the trigger for the NDX drop. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.reading: The Fed is hiking rather than cutting
macro_indicators.interpretation: Cited as a headwind to the bull case for continued dip-buying in leveraged Nasdaq products.
The drop on US-Iran talk hopes did not support equities, and the Nasdaq 100 still closed in correction.

risk_factors: Leveraged ETF rebalancing sales into the close amplify declines when the Nasdaq keeps falling.
Retail dip-buyers hold losses after the NDX entered correction, while professionals have already de-risked.
The Fed is hiking rather than cutting.
Leverage elsewhere in the system, with levered ETFs described as the tip of the iceberg per Simon White.
Reversing EM and Brazil retail flows.
Continued supply in miners and copper-linked equities.
vol_and_positioning: Levered ETFs took in a record +$13B in October, including $3B on Friday, the largest daily inflow YTD. The article estimates a $35B rebalancing sale into Friday's close, per Nomura.
Levered long ETFs historically take in about 50bps of prior-day AUM on -2σ Nasdaq days and bleed modestly on +2σ days. Inverse ETFs show the reverse pattern.
Goldman's Coppersmith reports the biggest plunge in professional risk appetite in 5 years, against record retail triple-levered buying.

Because 3x ETFs rebalance daily, each down day forces more selling of the underlying near the close. The article says the next leg lower is likely to be decided around 3:50pm by these rebalancing flows.
A record $7B went into SOXL in a single week during the SOX's worst week of the year, as noted in an earlier piece.
Retail flows into Asia are showing cracks, with Korea seeing $2.6B of retail selling last week.
geopolitical: US-Iran talk hopes drove oil down more than 7% on Monday.
Brazil ETF inflows have started to reverse after the Brazilian election.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Lucas sees 'records in the making' continuing. $1.7T of steady YTD ETF inflows is large buying power, and levered ETF buyers have been right to buy every crash for five years.
tension_points.bear_case: Professional risk appetite saw its biggest plunge in five years, the Fed is hiking, and the funds with the biggest October inflows are the ones that fell the most. Friday's record levered buying is already underwater and 3x units rebalance lower each afternoon the Nasdaq falls.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further Nasdaq 100 declines after the 10% correction, which force lower daily rebalancing of the 3x units built over the past three weeks.

theme_stances.key_argument: Retail buying of 3x products into the selloff leaves rebalancing flows, not fundamentals, setting the next leg lower.
theme_stances.evidence: buying the dip works great, right up until the dip has a dip.

theme_stances.key_argument: Money leaving the AI trade went into health care, which had its best month since April 2020.
theme_stances.evidence: which is what an orderly defensive rotation looks like
